contentHtml:
The Laguna de la Media Luna (Half Moon Lagoon) is a system of freshwater springs in Rioverde, San Luis Potosí, where the water reaches up to 28 °C year-round and underwater visibility tops 30 meters. Its name describes its shape exactly: a curve about 500 meters long that resembles the outline of a half moon. For many travelers exploring the Huasteca Potosina, the question that comes up before planning the trip is whether the destination is worth the detour from the main route — and the answer is yes, especially if scuba diving or snorkeling is high on your list. Rioverde is a city of just over 100,000 people in the central region (zona media) of San Luis Potosí, a transition zone between the semi-arid highlands and the lush tropical Huasteca, which explains why this freshwater oasis surprises first-time visitors so much.

This guide brings together everything you need to know about the Media Luna Lagoon in 2026: up-to-date Media Luna prices by activity, verified opening hours, Media Luna diving options with a certified guide, and the most efficient route from Ciudad Valles. According to local operators who work the site regularly, the park received more than 80,000 visitors in 2025, with peaks between December and March, when the outside temperature makes the thermal waters especially appealing.

At www.huasteca-potosina.com we work with local guides and operators in the region. This guide is updated with real experiences from people who travel the Huasteca Potosina every week. Last updated: October 2026. If you want to plan your trip with everything taken care of, check out the all-inclusive packages to visit the Media Luna Lagoon.

The Media Luna Lagoon: What It Is, Where It Is, and Why the Water Looks Like That

Why Is the Water at the Media Luna Lagoon So Clear and Warm?

The Media Luna Lagoon is fed by springs that rise straight up from the limestone subsoil of the Potosí plain. The water filters for years through limestone, which removes sediment and keeps it at a constant 28 °C, regardless of the season. This combination — stable temperature, a visible bottom, and no strong currents — makes it one of the best places in Mexico for beginner divers.

The travelers we coordinate to the area report an experience very different from the lagoons and rivers of the sierra: here there's no turbulence or vegetation blocking your view. The white sand bottom and the light that reaches all the way down to the spring's source create almost aquarium-like conditions. Book the Discover Scuba Diving at the Laguna de la Media Luna tour if you want to experience that dive with a PADI-certified instructor, from $1,300 MXN per person.

Wildlife and the Underwater Ecosystem: What You'll See Below the Surface

The Media Luna Lagoon is home to the softshell turtle (Apalone spinifera) and the endemic fish Cichlasoma bartoni, both protected species. Divers who descend between 5 and 10 meters find colonies of these turtles resting on the walls of the main spring, a sight that's hard to find anywhere else in the Huasteca Potosina.

The presence of sensitive wildlife is one reason the park limits the number of divers in the water at once and requires a certified guide for deeper dives. If you're interested in the broader ecological context of the region's springs, the article on the Nacimiento de Huichihuayán (the Huichihuayán spring) offers a useful comparison with another spring system in the area.

Activities and Media Luna Prices for 2026: Diving, Snorkeling, and More

Media Luna Diving: Certified Options and What Each One Includes

First-time visitors to the Media Luna Lagoon often can't decide between diving with the park's in-house school or hiring an outside agency. In 2026, the park's official school offers a package that covers full gear, photos, video, and a professional guide for $1,350 MXN per person. It's the most affordable option and is enough for an introductory dive. For more experienced divers, or anyone looking for more technical equipment, ecotourism agencies in the area charge around $2,100 MXN per person with professional gear.

Our Discover Scuba Diving at the Laguna de la Media Luna tour costs $1,300 MXN per person and includes an orientation with a PADI-certified instructor, practice in shallow water, and a dive to 5 to 10 meters — the ideal depth to see the turtles and the spring's source without needing prior certification. See available tours in the Huasteca Potosina if you want to combine this experience with other destinations in the region.

How Much Is Admission to the Media Luna Lagoon in 2026?

General admission to the Media Luna Lagoon costs $150 MXN per person in 2026. Camping inside the park is paid separately: $150 MXN per tent, no matter the size of the tent or how many people use it. Snorkeling and the open swimming areas are included in general admission at no extra charge.

If you're bringing family or a large group, the camping fee is a great deal: four people in a single tent pay the same $150 MXN as one person alone. Bring cash, because services inside the park don't always take cards. If you want to compare budgets for other similar destinations in the region, the article on how much it costs to visit the Huasteca Potosina gives you a full overview by destination.

Practical Tips Before Visiting the Media Luna Lagoon

Planning your visit to the Media Luna Lagoon well makes the difference between enjoying it at a relaxed pace and arriving when the park is packed. These are the things the travelers we work with learn — sometimes the hard way — before coming back a second time.

  • Confirm the hours before you leave: Current sources list hours of 8:00 a.m. to 6:30 p.m., Monday through Sunday, although another source says it's closed on Tuesdays and open only until 5:00 p.m. The discrepancy is real: call the park directly the day before or check its official social media to confirm.
  • Arrive between 9:00 and 11:00 a.m.: That's the window when sunlight enters the water at the best angle for diving and snorkeling, and the park hasn't reached peak crowds yet. On weekends from December to March, there can be a line at the entrance starting at 10:00 a.m.
  • Pack a change of clothes and an extra towel: The water is warm, but the wind when you get out can make it feel colder. If you plan to dive and also swim, bring two sets of clothes; the changing area has limited space. Look over the packing checklist for the jungle of San Luis Potosí so you don't forget anything.
  • Use biodegradable sunscreen or none at all: The park restricts regular sunscreen to protect the endemic wildlife. Some visitors skip sunscreen altogether, since the water has color and much of the activity happens below the surface.
  • Minimum cash budget per person: Plan on at least $500 MXN if you're only swimming ($150 MXN admission + food in the park). If you add diving with the in-house school, the budget goes up to at least $1,500 MXN. The nearest ATM is in the city of Rioverde, about 15 minutes away by car. The park has a dining area where you can eat enchiladas potosinas (the state's signature chile-tinted enchiladas) or regional snacks for $80 to $150 MXN per plate, which helps you better estimate the day's total spending.

How Do You Get to the Media Luna Lagoon from Ciudad Valles?

The Media Luna Lagoon is in the municipality of Rioverde, in the central region of San Luis Potosí, outside the usual mountain circuit of the Huasteca Potosina. That makes it a detour you need to plan on purpose, but the trip is worth it. The groups we coordinate from Ciudad Valles to the lagoon report travel times of 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours, depending on traffic on federal highway 70.

Main Route: Ciudad Valles to Media Luna in Rioverde by Car

The distance between Ciudad Valles and the Media Luna Lagoon is 122 kilometers on paved road. The most direct route takes Federal Highway 70 toward Rioverde, and from the junction in the city there are signs to the park. The Ciudad Valles–Rioverde stretch has no toll booths, and the road is in good condition along most of the way in 2026. From the state capital, San Luis Potosí, the distance is about 110 kilometers, or 1 hour 20 minutes on the toll highway. Book the Discover Scuba Diving at the Laguna de la Media Luna tour if you'd rather not worry about transportation logistics.

What Can You Combine with the Media Luna Lagoon on the Same Day or Weekend?

You can see the Media Luna Lagoon in half a day, which leaves time to combine it with the Tamtoc archaeological site or a food stop in Rioverde. If you're planning a full weekend from Ciudad Valles, the natural itinerary is to spend Saturday at the lagoon and Sunday at the Micos Waterfalls (Cascadas de Micos) on the way back. Frequently Asked Questions About the Media Luna Lagoon

Do I need a diving certification to dive at the Media Luna Lagoon?

No. The park's school and our tour offer introductory diving with a PADI-certified instructor for people with no prior experience. The dive goes to 5 to 10 meters deep, after practice in shallow water, following the park's 2026 safety protocols.

How much do admission and diving cost at the Media Luna Lagoon in 2026?

General admission costs $150 MXN per person. Diving with the park's in-house school costs $1,350 MXN per person and includes gear, photos, and video. Outside agencies charge around $2,100 MXN. Our tour is priced at $1,300 MXN per person with a PADI instructor.

Which cities make it easy to get to Media Luna in Rioverde?

From Ciudad Valles it's 122 km on Federal Highway 70, a drive of about 2 hours. From the state capital, San Luis Potosí, it's around 110 km, about 80 minutes on the highway. The road is paved and in good condition in 2026, with no tolls on the main stretch.

Is the Media Luna Lagoon safe for kids and families?

Yes. The open swimming areas are shallow near the shore, and the still water makes it suitable for children with adult supervision. For Media Luna diving, minors need to confirm the minimum age with the operator (usually 10 years old). Bring water shoes to walk around the entry areas; the bottom can have exposed rock.

Can you camp at the Media Luna Lagoon, and what facilities are available?

Yes, the park allows camping on its grounds. The cost is $150 MXN per tent, regardless of how many people share it. The camping area has restrooms, cold-water showers, and a designated campfire area. It's best to arrive before 4:00 p.m. to secure a spot in high season (December to March), since spaces are limited and assigned on a first-come, first-served basis.
